review_text: I’ve had these headphones for a year now since I bought them. I am an avid runner and use them at the gym. They have been great and are only just now giving issues with retaining battery life. Before, I could use them for an average of 2-3 workouts (averaging an hour each time) before needing to charge them. Sometimes I would forget and walk away from my phone and they had about a 15-20 foot range before losing signal. They don’t take long to charge to full power again and sit on my ears wonderfully, even for the most intensive workouts.  I would highly recommend them for the price and anyone looking for a great set of starting Bluetooth headphones.

Have been debating on upgrading my monitor setup for the past couple of months and finally settle with this. I originally had 2 AOC I2757 27" 1080p monitors and they worked but lacked in many areas, after one started having screen tearing issues I decided it was time to try something different. I originally toyed with a 4k system but either due to most having only a 30hz refresh rate or being extremely expensive if they do have a 60hz rate, I shied away from those option. I also looked into 144hz monitors because I like to game every so often, I turned those down due to all are tn based panels and eventually wanting a dual monitor setup again I turned them down also. That leads only two option I could go with ultra thin bezel 1080p setup or 1440, guess what won. I probably looked through 10 youtube reviews before I decided on this particular model, mainly due to all the right options: matte screen, matte bezel, vesa mount(this sealed the deal), thin bezel, fully adjustable stand, great build quality. It's crazy that this monitor is almost a year old and still one of the best 1440 monitors. As far as hardware goes it does tax your video card quite a bit more. Gaming wise I would say you would need at least a 700 series card or 600 sli'd (no ideo on amd's sorry) to run this at medium + quality. I have a 690 and it handles everything on high pretty well, I tried titanfall on ultra and it started to get a little hairy and unplayable( I don't know if it was a driver issue or what). Overall great buy and will be buying another one in the future after I upgrade my video card.

Update: 31.07.19, I can't say enough about this camera. I've had it for several years and it is still my go to camera for most things photography related. I decided to post some photos I took. Truth be told they aren't straight out of the camera. I use PS6, Photomatix, and Topaz to edit my photos, mostly PS and Photomatix. Photomatix merges the three exposures into a blended JPEG and then I use PS6 to bring all the photos together. The valley photo was over a hundred photos and it took my computer over four hours to process the image and then I had to edit the composite. It was worth the effort. I bought this camera before I left on my trip. I pushed its limits to the max. Yes, it is a point and shoot but it has many features of a pro camera which fits in your jacket or sweater pocket.
I spent a month in Germany with this camera and I found it to be great in most cases. I did some research about this camera and picked one up about a week before I left on my trip. I left my 5D2 at home and did most of my photos with this camera. I made a conscious decision to travel as light as possible for my trip. If I were to do it over again I'd just take this camera and maybe a lighter tripod and my computer and that would be my kit. On this trip, my camera bag with all the gear, cameras (the Fuji X-20 and NEX 5R), computer, chargers and cables was right at 20 lbs. My last foray was with 40D and three lenses, plus a computer and cables had my camera bag was over 50 lbs. I used this camera to make Vertoramas and it worked out well for me. By using vertoramas I didn't need a wide-angle lens if I wanted a wide shot that was more detailed than the panorama mode could make. If you don't know what a Vertorama is it is composite several photos merged together to make one photo. I shot all of the photos I took in +1,0,-1 bracketed exposures. I would have liked to do a +2,0,-2 configuration but the Fuji camera can't do the spread. It was a minor point.
The pano shots in the camera of 120, 180 and 360 can be nice but the 180 and 360 are very difficult to complete handheld.
This camera fit in my sweater/jacket pocket easily so I was able to take it everywhere without any difficulty. It was handy. I'm not such a big fan of the twisting of the lens to turn the camera on. I've adapted.
I used this camera and took over 7000 photos and videos in a month. I'm not so critical about the video capability of the camera as I usually just use videos as sound bites. I did notice that the video I made of a passing train lost focus for a few seconds but came back rather quickly.
I used the camera in all sorts of weather and had a heart-stopping moment when it slipped off of my wrist and hit the pavement. I had a lanyard but for some reason, it didn't catch my hand at all the camera just went straight to the ground and bounced several times. I retrieved it and turned it on and it worked just fine. I'm still taking photos with the camera without any issues. The camera has a little ding at one corner and the lens cap also has a couple of scratches on the edges to show that it hit the ground but that's it. So it is built pretty solid.
I bought a third party lens hood and while it worked well I tended to not use it because I wasn't able to put the lens cap back on without taking off the lens hood.
I like the Image Quality of this camera. I found the colors to be very nice and pleasing. Then again I use the Velvia film mode while taking photos with this camera. I use Velvia film with my 4x5 camera and this camera is pretty close to that film.
After using a full-frame camera for several years the file size of the X-20 seem rather small but the image quality is still very good.
You can use this as a basic point and shoot camera and it does very well. I like I was able to use RAW(RAF for Fuji) files with the camera although the JPEG images are good quality I've been working with RAW so long that I just prefer the latitude with the type file.
I don't miss the weight of the heavy DSLR. This may be a very small camera but it takes great images in most conditions. The auto ISO is 800 and that works well mostly. In really low light situations you will start seeing noise in the dark areas of a photo. This can be corrected if you use PS6 or some other Noise reduction program. So again for me, it isn't an issue.
The range of the lens is good. I'd prefer a little wider and longer but then it wouldn't be the same camera then. I adapted by getting a little closer for those portrait shots and shooting several shots and merging them together for the wide-angle shots I wanted.
The camera has several different Modes to play with but I typically don't use any of them simply because they tend to switch the camera to JPEG mode and I want the RAW file.
I bought a couple of extra batteries for this camera and was surprised that I spent one day where I took over 700 photos on one battery. Then again they were mostly three bracket shots so one press of the shutter the camera took three photos.
Conclusion:
For me, this camera is the reason my Canon gear hasn't been out of the bag in years. They seem to have the best sensor of any camera out there currently.
Tip:
Most electronic gear today is dual voltage so you don't have to get a converter. I bought some plug adapters for this trip and when I got to Germany I went to a hardware store and bought a power strip. I knew where there was a hardware store so for me that wasn't a problem to find.

Overall I like this camera. I read other reviews which implied that the construction is flimsly, but I disagree. The camera is compact but solid, and is a good value.

Photograph quality was quite good; I have a few Canon point & shoot cameras (and my wife has a Nikon), and this one matches those for image quality. It also is a bit more automatic than most that I've used before; it chooses modes like landscape, portrait, macro, and night shot automatically based on focal distance and lighting. That was a pleasant surprise.

There were two problems, however. The first (which is minor) is that the camera uses micro-SD cards, and does not ship with one. It may be a worthwhile trade-off to use the smaller cards (smaller camera), but the cards are difficult to install and remove due to both their size, and their propensity to go in "crooked". On a related plus, the camera does seem to have a small amount of on-board memory, but that seemed enough for just a few snapshots.

The more significant problem I had was related to the camera's videos and the Mac OS X environment. I'm using a brand new iMac with the latest OS, and every time I connected the camera (or inserted the card into the Mac) with any video on it, my two media-related Mac OS apps (iMovie and Aperture) would hang. This only happened when the camera/card contained video. Additionally, the video quality was not quite up to par (somewhat jumpy).

I used the camera under water without any problems. It's a nice feature that also allows you to not worry so much when carrying your camera around on vacation and around water. Overall--a good point & shoot, and if I were able to resolve the Mac integration issues I'd have rated this four stars.
